query: For structural materials intended for fusion plasma-facing components, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness, and why? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to an unperturbed baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in structural materials for fusion plasma-facing components are governed by the formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters.
generation.intervention: Irradiation with helium ions at high temperatures
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 500-1000°C, Helium ion fluence: 10^20 - 10^22 ions/m²
generation.mechanism: Helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility enhance plastic strain and toughness by reducing the energy required for dislocation glide
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased high-temperature plastic strain and toughness compared to unirradiated material
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 500-1000°C, Helium ion fluence: 10^20 - 10^22 ions/m²
generation.uncertainty: Lack of direct experimental evidence for helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility at high temperatures

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of irradiated and unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: No significant difference in high-temperature plastic strain and toughness between irradiated and unirradiated samples
